nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We should get going...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Do we have enough time to get back?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Actually, I have a confession to make...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What is it?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We have quite a bit of time to get back. I budgeted a little bit extra because I thought you might want to drive us home.
Nick flips his keys over to Sara.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You're serious?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: In a 'I hope I won't regret this later,' kind of way, yeah.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You're the best! `Eeee!`

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Love?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Er... I mean...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I didn't say anything about love.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I know, that's not what I meant...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Are you saying that you love me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No! Not that I... I...
Sara takes a deep breath.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Can we forget about what I just said?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah... I guess.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Thanks.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Normally, I'd agree. But this is... Different.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What do you mean?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I don't know... It's like there's something about how I am when I'm with you, Sara.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's like I'm less nervous. More... Myself.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I feel like I can tell you anything.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Awww. That's like the sweetest thing anyone's ever said to me.
Sara leans up and kisses Nick!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Telling someone what?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know, about feelings you have, like love.
Sara loses her balance, falling into the sand!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: `Oof!`
Nick comes running up...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Is that how it's supposed to look? Kind of like a spider having a seizure?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No... I guess I'm out of practice.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That's okay. I can use the photo I took for a project I've been working on... The theme is humans acting like bugs.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Great... Just what a girl wants to hear. That she's perfect for her boyfriend's bug collage.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Heh. Sorry. Didn't mean to put it like that.
Nick checks his phone...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We've only got twenty seven more minutes! What else can we do?
Sara sticks the landing!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: `I did it!`
Nick comes running up, embracing her tightly!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That looked so cool!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Did you get the photo?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I got a perfect shot with just a little bit of blur so you can really `see` the motion...
nodes.text_bbcode: I got a perfect shot with just a little bit of blur so you can really [color=#e23b3b][i]see[/i][/color] the motion...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Check it out.
Nick shows Sara the photo... Sara's form is perfect... She looks like the spoke in a bicycle wheel.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Beautiful.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You mean me? Or the picture?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Oh, I definitely mean you.
He leans down and kisses her. After a long time, they part...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: As much I'd love doing that forever, I think we should do more here at the beach than just make out and do cartwheels.
Nick shakes his hips again...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: { My cartwheel brings all the girls to the beach! {

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay. Yes. I'll do anything if it means you not doing that.
For the rest of their short time together, Sara and Nick cram in as much fun as they can...
They build sand castles...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: We should have a moat!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Typical Kessler. Trying to set up a place where she can swim.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Do I need to mention how you converted the dungeon into a dark room?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: They're practically the same thing!
They collect shells...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Look how pretty this is!
Nick takes a picture. She looks at it.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick! This is just a picture of me! Get one of my shell too!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Okay, okay, fine, Miss Bossy.
And Nick buries Sara's legs in the sand, forcing her to close her eyes as he works on something.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't know if this qualifies as fun...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Just give me a minute... Aaaaaand... Open!
Sara opens her eyes. Nick has constructed a long tail out of sand, extending from Sara's waist.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You make for one heck of a mermaid.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee...
He takes a picture.
An alarm on his phone goes off.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Time to go...
Nick lifts Sara out of the sand, and the two of them head toward the car...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Sara, I... I want to tell you something.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's about the way I feel about you...
Sara blushes.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's just... I've never felt this way about anyone.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm... I'm feeling the same way.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And... Uh... And... Yeah. That's it.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, I'm really glad you said that. It isn't easy telling someone...
Sara's legs swing down toward the ground, propelling her upright again...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Stay balanced!
When her feet touch the sand, she...
Sara maintains her balance, kicking off with her legs.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yes!
As momentum carries her legs over her body, she...
The car starts to turn toward the lamppost...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Watch out!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I am watching out!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Go around the post!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's what I'm trying to do!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You're headed right for it!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No, I'm not!
Sara turns the wheel sharply, but Nick reaches out and pulls it the other way!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Look out!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Let go!
`Bump.` The car nudges up against the lamppost with an imperceptible impact.
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Bump.[/b] The car nudges up against the lamppost with an imperceptible impact.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Why were you yelling at me?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: One, I wasn't yelling! And two, you weren't following any of my instructions!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I... I know... I think I just got a little too excited. Do you think the car is damaged?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: No. You're fine. That's why they call them bumpers after all.
In the distance, dark clouds begin to form in the sky...
Sara turns the wheel smoothly...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Good. Good. Good.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Like I said... Easy.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Turn.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You need to turn here!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh!
Sara turns the wheel...
The car moves closer to the lamppost.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What do you do now?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: This part's easy...
Sara grips the steering wheel tight, and...
Sara floors the gas pedal! The car lurches forward!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Whoa! Whoa! Whoa!
Sara immediately stomps on the brake!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What happened?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Just, um, testing the sensitivity...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And my heart rate... Can you keep it under 100 miles an hour inside the parking lot?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... Sorry...
Sara presses down on the gas pedal, this time much softer... The car glides forward.
Sara floors the gas pedal! The car lurches forward!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Whoa! Whoa! Whoa!
Sara immediately stomps on the brake!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What happened?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Just, um, testing the sensitivity...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And my heart rate... Can you keep it under 100 miles an hour inside the parking lot?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... Sorry...
Sara presses down on the gas pedal, this time much softer... The car glides forward.
Sara floors the gas pedal! The car lurches forward!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Whoa! Whoa! Whoa!
Sara immediately stomps on the brake!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What happened?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Just, um, testing the sensitivity...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And my heart rate... Can you keep it under 100 miles an hour inside the parking lot?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... Sorry...
Sara presses down on the gas pedal, this time much softer... The car glides forward.
She presses down lightly on the gas pedal, gliding forward.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hahaha! I'm driving!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What do I do?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Uh... Go?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh yeah, right.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: All right, the engine's on... Now what?
Sara grips the steering wheel and...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I think I'm supposed to... Check... Something.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Nope. Were you listening to me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I was, I swear! I'm just a little overeager...
Sara turns the engine on.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I think I'm supposed to... Check... Something.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Nope. Were you listening to me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I was, I swear! I'm just a little overeager...
Sara turns the engine on.
Sara turns the key in the ignition...
`Prrr!` The engine hums.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: All right...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee hee! Power!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Uh, scale it back there, Commander McWheels.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I think I'm supposed to... Check... Something.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Nope. Were you listening to me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I was, I swear! I'm just a little overeager...
Sara turns the engine on.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What's the next step?
Sara thinks about it for a second and...
Sara checks the mirrors, making sure she has proper visibility.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Good. I'm glad you remembered that step.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Did you ever doubt?
Sara moves to start the car.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Mirrors. Don't forget your mirrors.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, whoops.
Sara checks her mirrors.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You don't want to find out that your mirrors are messed up while you're on the freeway.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I know. I know.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh... What do I do?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, yeah, `now` I start the car.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What's next?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Next, I...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Aren't you forgetting something?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, right. The seatbelt. Sorry.
Sara sheepishly puts her seatbelt on.
Sara reaches over and pulls her seatbelt on.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Nice start.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Safety first, right?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Uh... Sara?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Sorry, I just blanked on what the first step was. But I got it.
Sara moves to turn the key in the ignition...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Phew! That was close... I wish I didn't have to lie to my dad like this...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But seeing Nick is important to me...
After practice the next day, Sara climbs into Nick's car...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: So where to? We could go to the mall, the beach... There's a hiking trail I've wanted to visit...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Actually, Nick... Could you... Could you teach me how to drive?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Are you sure? I mean, your dad...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Is not here. Come on, it's overdue. I should have taken my driver's test months ago.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm convinced he's never going to teach me.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I'll see what we can do...
Nick drives Sara into the school parking lot...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay, okay, I'm like the last girl to squeal about something exciting, but...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm `so` excited that you're teaching me how to drive! `Eeeeeeee!`
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] excited that you're teaching me how to drive! [color=#3b78e2][i]Eeeeeeee![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I wish I had recorded that sound on my phone. I feel like I just witnessed something rare, like seeing Bigfoot or something.
Nick parks the car in an isolated area of the lot. He takes a deep breath.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Okay... I know you're excited, but that's kind of the last thing I need you to be right now.
Sara forces a serious look onto her face.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Got it. I'm not excited.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Really?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Really. Look at my face.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Just kidding! Let's do this!
Sara hops out of the car, bounding around it toward the driver's seat.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: `Eee! Eee! Eee!`
Nick slides over to the passenger seat as Sara hops in.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Oh boy.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What do we do first? Open 'er up?! Pedal to the metal?! Burn rubber?!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah. None of that. We're going to start with...
Nick points out a lamppost fifty yards away.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: ...That. Let's try to turn around that before we, you know, flash the dash or whatever.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Flash the dash?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Just sub in an appropriate car term, okay?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Got it.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: So, turning around the post... That's your job. My job is not to lose my cool while guiding you through it.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee. Okay. I'm ready. What do I do?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's pretty simple. Just a couple of steps...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Obviously, put your seatbelt on...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Start the car...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Oh and make sure to check your mirrors before you start the car, don't forget that.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Then press gently on the accelerator...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And when the time is right, turn the wheel smoothly.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I think I can do all that.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Good. Ready?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Ready!
Sara takes a deep, excited breath and...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Is that so?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yup. You're an old guy, Dad. And I'm, you know, `The Machine.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Yup. You're an old guy, Dad. And I'm, you know, [color=#3b78e2][i]The Machine.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Ha! I might have to up your training regiment if you're this cocky.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm just kidding. We must have just missed each other.
Sara's dad smiles at her as she heads upstairs to her room.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: But you just said you took the same route?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I did. Except for this one shortcut I found.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hmmm... I don't know if I like the idea of you taking shortcuts.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What do you mean?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: It isn't safe, for one. And it spreads laziness. No more shortcuts, got it?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah. Fine. No more shortcuts.
Sara's dad gives her a curious look as she heads upstairs to her room.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: How are you doing? You're practicing a lot.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah, it seems like I'm working harder and harder. And my little sister is part of it too.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: All we ever do as a family anymore is train.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: My dad won't let me go out anymore.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: And I can forget about learning how to drive. He thinks it's too dangerous. I can't go anywhere without his permission...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: It's like he controls every aspect of my life...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, not `every` aspect... You're with me now, aren't you?
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, not [color=#e23b3b][i]every[/i][/color] aspect... You're with me now, aren't you?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... I think I'll 'run home' after swim practice every day...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I think you should too...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And I promise you... We are going to have so much fun this summer.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm going to hold you to that.
Nick chuckles and takes her hand.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You know, Sara... I really like you...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I really like you too...
Nick pulls her in for a kiss right before they head out.
Sara comes home from the amusement park, now dressed in her running clothes...
As she crosses toward the stairs, her dad calls to her from the kitchen.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: How was your run?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Good. Good. Real good.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You take a different route?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No... Same route. Why?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: After I dropped off your sister, I came back to keep you company. You know, see if you could compete with your old man.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: But I didn't see you...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, that's probably because...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You pretty much know the gist of what I'm doing.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: When I'm not working on yearbook...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I'm taking candids of you!
Nick snaps a picture of Sara taking a bite out of a purple-colored scoop.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You'd better not print these!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: What if I promise only I get to see them?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Arguably worse.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: But really, if you want to know about my photography...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I'm saving up for the Kikon 220 Telephoto lens. It's expensive, but it has multi-layer lens coating that reduces flare and ghosting...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's... Cool.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And it's got constant fast maximum aperture throughout the entire zoom range... And...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: This is boring you, isn't it? It goes against my personality type to be boring, so...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Sure... What do you want to know?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Whatever you want to tell me.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: All I know is that you don't have a parent that hangs around you pretty much every hour of the day.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, I don't have your kind of talent.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Maybe if photography were a national sport, my dad would hang around me all the time.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: When I was younger, my parents were really interested in taking me places.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We went on a lot of day trips to museums, movies, and art galleries...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I remember the summer right after eighth grade, we went to an art gallery devoted entirely to photographs.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: My mother chose it because she used to take pictures.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That was the moment I really became aware of how beautiful pictures could really be.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's pretty awesome.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah. It was. Unfortunately, that was one of the last trips.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: After I started high school, I was staying in Spartan Academy's dorms... So we didn't see each other as often.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: At least now that I'm at Twin Branches, I see them around.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Thank you for sharing that with me.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Thanks for asking.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, it's always nice to learn more about you...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Hey, I think we have a few minutes to grab some ice cream on the way out if you're up for it...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I love ice cream!
They enter Clown Cones and stare up at a bright yellow-and-red board of flavors.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's on me. What's your favorite?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: To be honest, I don't actually remember... It's been a long time since I've had any.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Ice cream isn't exactly on my dad's healthy foods list.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Don't worry about it. I know exactly what we're going to get...
A few minutes later, Nick brings Sara a gigantic bowl of ice cream!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Here's their Clown Car special! Thirty-two scoops in one slightly freaky, slightly funny, clown-faced bowl!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What am I going to do with thirty-two scoops?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: If you take a bite out of all of them, you'll figure out what your favorite is!
Sara takes a bite out of a lime-green scoop and wrinkles her face.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Apparently, I don't like key lime.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: One down, thirty-one to go!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, I can't eat all this in ten minutes!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Heh, I'll be helping too!
They dig into the ice cream.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know, of all the flavors, I like peppermint the most.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Really? No one likes peppermint.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, I do! I like the candied mint pieces... And besides, it's pink.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, `that` changes everything.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee hee...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm glad you took me here. It's been a long time since I've gone to a fair and eaten ice cream!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: My family doesn't really do this kind of stuff anymore.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah... I know what that's like. That's kind of why I had to pick up photography as a hobby.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I wonder what he means by that... I don't want to pry, but...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, Nick, tell me something about your...
They fall in line for Crazy Coaster, and soon they're at the front.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I didn't know you liked roller coasters.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've gone on smaller coasters when I was a kid, but never on something like this. It looks so cool!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm a little nervous, though. Is it scary?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Only if you're afraid of heights.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: ...Actually, I'm really afraid of heights!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Wrong thing to say then, huh?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh-huh...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We can still back out...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No way. We only have time for one ride. I can do this. It's fun, right?
They step up to the ride, and an attendant straps them into the seats. Nick grabs her hand.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Just squeeze if you get nervous, okay?
The ride starts! Sara's stomach lurches badly with every twist, turn, and fall!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Ahhhhh!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You're squeezing too tight!
They step off the ride a minute later.
Sara drops onto a park bench, putting her head down, while Nick shakes out his bruised hand.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Sorry about your hand... I got scared.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Hey, that's what I'm here for. Hand-holding, moral support, and a general reminder never to let you go on a roller coaster again...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... I think I'll stick with the kiddie coasters next time.
They fall in line for the Ferris wheel, and soon they are on their way to the top.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I hope you're not afraid of heights...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I kind of am, actually...
Sara sees the ground retreating. Her stomach turns a little.
Nick puts a hand on her shoulder, and she looks into his eyes.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Pro tip... Don't look down.
He puts an arm around her, and Sara leans into him.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: This is nice... I'm barely even thinking about how high up we are...
At the top, the Ferris wheel stops, and Sara and Nick have a view of the entire city.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I can see our school! And the lake... And my house!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Our city's pretty small from here, huh?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah, it's funny like that... It's so beautiful...
Nick pulls out a slim camera from his pocket and takes a picture of the cityscape.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Do you always bring your camera everywhere?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I like to have pictures. It reminds me of all the places I've gone...
Nick snaps a quick candid of Sara.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: ...And all the amazing people I've met.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, I wasn't ready for that!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And yet, you still look great.
He leans into a slow kiss, and Sara can feel herself relax, as the Ferris wheel descends.
They get off the ride.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: So you like Ferris wheels...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Anyway, let's head back. We'll have dinner, and then it's an early bedtime for you girls. We have a grueling weight lifting regimen in the morning.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Into the car, girls.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, Dad, I'm going to go for a run. I'll meet you back at the house, okay?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What? But that's an hour's run from here.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You have the energy for that? I feel like my legs are dead weight.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I think the practice will be good for me.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Well, I really admire your dedication. Come on, Emily. We'll see your sister at home.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And that is exactly how you have to be to win. You have to be able to push forward when you're really tired.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Oh...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: It's okay, Emily... You'll work up to it.
Emily and Coach Kessler get into the van. Sara waits until she sees her dad pull out of the lot.
Then she takes off down a path into the woods...
And a short ways away, she finds Nick!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: There you are. I wasn't sure you were going to make it today.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: How long do I have you for?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: It usually takes me an hour to finish my run, so that's all we have time for... Sorry.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I'm just happy I get to see you. You're always in practice.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I know... Ever since I broke that record, my dad's been pushing me harder and harder.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I hate sneaking around him like this, but it's the only way we'll ever hang out.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Hey, cheer up. We have one hour with each other. Let's make the most of it...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What can we do in an hour?
A few minutes later, they arrive at the fairgrounds.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I didn't even know the fair was in town!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I drove by it on the way up. This is the perfect thing for us.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Let's get on a ride!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, since we only have an hour... We can only do one. Which do you want?
Sara looks around and sees that the closest rides are the roller coaster and the Ferris wheel.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Let's get on the...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: She's entitled to it.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Fun? Sara, you know as well as I do that `fun` had nothing to do with your breaking the national record.
nodes.text_bbcode: Fun? Sara, you know as well as I do that [color=#e23b3b][i]fun[/i][/color] had nothing to do with your breaking the national record.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Well, no, it didn't really...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But all the pressure you put on me to win the race didn't help me break the national record either.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Remember how terrible I was at all the practices before the race?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I just needed to relax, and then I did great!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I guess.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: She'd just finished a hard sprint.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: And every hard-working athlete needs a few moments to relax and regroup.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know that.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That is a valid point...
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm glad you agree.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hey!
Coach Kessler storms up to the girls.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Knock it off. You're athletes, not girls.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Actually, Dad, I think we're both.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Hee hee.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's not funny. This is `training.`

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And Emily, you especially need to be focused.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What are you doing just standing there?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Sorry, Dad.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, we just finished our laps.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: So you just decided to stand around? There's always work to be done.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Emily, you especially need to focus on your swimming.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You won't be breaking any records like your sister unless you start being more serious about yourself.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I know... I'm sorry.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You don't need to yell at her, Dad.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Why not?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Because...
Sara bends down, scoops up some of the water from the lake, and hurls it at Emily!
Emily squeals and dodges Sara's attempts to splash her.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ha ha ha! Hey, stop that!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Not until you stop being so serious all the time!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Okay, okay! I promise!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's more like it!
Sara does nothing. Sara looks silently out over the water as Emily broods.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've never been good at comforting other people...
He touches his forehead to hers.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I love the way you laugh... The way your eyes narrow when you're upset...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I love how you make me feel...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I love being around you...
Sara's heart lifts.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I love you, Sara Kessler.
Sara kisses Nick, throwing her entire heart into it.
They only part for air when Nick's phone buzzes a couple minutes later.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Looks like it's time for us to go.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Looks like.
Back on the beach surrounding the lake, Sara takes Nick's keys.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'll drive us.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's starting to rain. Are you sure?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've been practicing enough. I think I can handle it. It's just a drizzle.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Everyone needs to drive through their first rainstorm, I guess.
Sara climbs into the driver's seat, puts the car into gear, and starts driving down the road.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Which route should I take?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Let's take the back road around the lake...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: The road winds around a river, and there are some good pictures I can take from there.
Sara pulls onto the road while Nick takes pictures.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Any good photos?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: No. It's raining too hard.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You can't take pictures in the rain?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I don't have the right lens. Besides, this isn't just any rain... It's a storm.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, maybe I shouldn't have insisted on driving...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's okay... You know what to do. Just stay calm and...
Nick stops, seeing an oil slick in the road.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Sara, watch out!
His warning comes too late. He sucks in his breath as the car glides over the slick and slips.
Sara loses her hold on the wheel, and the car spins out of control!
The car skids off the road, punches through the guardrails, and careens off the embankment...
And Sara begins to experience everything simultaneously...
She sees Nick yell her name and reach out for her...
She feels her stomach lift as if on a roller coaster when the car overturns once...
Twice...
She hears the sound of wrenching metal and crunching glass and smells gasoline, the summer rain, and blood...
She looks back at Nick one last time, her lips curling into a smile as she recalls the few minutes before when he'd said he loved her...
A few seconds later, the car comes to a hard stop in the stream below...
And all is still.

args.text: Surviving High School
Thanks for playing!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well, that about sums it up.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You beat me to it.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: So you aren't going to say it back?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I love you too.
Sara tries to speak, but she chokes up!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You're not making this easy...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: But I'm going to say it...
Nick gives her a kiss on the cheek.
Then he takes Sara's hand, and they climb the rest of the trail.
At the summit, they look out over the shimmering waters of the lake and the valley below.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, it's breathtaking.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Just like you.
She turns to look at him, and he draws her closer.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Sara... All this time we've been spending together...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's made me feel...
He stops, suddenly uncertain, and Sara feels her heart flutter in her chest.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No, let me...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: All right. Open your eyes!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's... A dandelion.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah! Make a wish and blow on the dandelion. And then your wish will come true!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Any wish I want?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Just don't waste it.
Nick thinks up his wish and blows on the flower. The seedlings waver in the wind and blow back into his face!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Ack! Blech! Blech!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Are you okay? I hope that's not what you wished for.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah, I'm fine.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Besides, I'm already pretty happy with what I have.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: All right. Open your eyes!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's... Flowers.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You don't like them?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I just wasn't expecting that. I love them.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Not to mention what they do as far as turning the tables on traditional gender roles.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's exactly what I was trying to do.
Sara turns to leave the room.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I should have told her about Nick...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: And she should know that I'm not a machine... I'm not perfect...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'll tell her tomorrow. After my date.
The next day, Sara meets Nick at their spot after her swim practice.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, so what are we doing today?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: There's a trail around here... I figured we could follow it to the top of the mountain.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: The very top? How are we going to get there in an hour?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's a very short mountain.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay. I trust you.
They take a trail that winds around the lake and up to the top.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: How was practice today?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: It was okay. My dad is increasing the amount of weight that I practice with, so that's been stressing me out.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You swim with weights?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yes. For resistance. That way when I swim without them, I fly through the water.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But my muscles are totally aching right now from the new load.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: If I'd known, I wouldn't have taken you uphill.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: No... This is great. This is my time to relax.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm always happy when I'm with you. I wish there was some way I could give you all you've given me.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Wait! I got it. Close your eyes...
Nick does so while Sara looks around for something to give him.
Near the trail, Sara spots a dandelion with a white tuft and a small burst of orange wildflowers.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Really? That's your big secret?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yep.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No, it's not!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What do you mean?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara, we get the same amount of sleep!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh yeah... We do, don't we?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: If you didn't feel like telling me, you didn't have to.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I'll figure it out on my own. Good night, Sara!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Night.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What do you mean? It's not like dad gives us any vacations.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Not a vacation, just a small break. Just some time where you do something for just you.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I try to do that, but it always makes me feel a little selfish.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sometimes, I feel guilty talking to Kimi on the phone for too long.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Well, you shouldn't.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What do you do for yourself?
Sara thinks of Nick.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh... I'll tell you when you're older.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Heh, okay! Thanks, Sara.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Now get to bed. I'll see you at practice tomorrow.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yep!
And for the rest of summer, Nick and Sara steal the hour after her practice and spend time together...
They look at shops at the mall...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I've discovered where independent thought and free will go to die.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But at least they die fashionably...
They pick flowers around the lake after her father drives off...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: My parents used to have a lake house, and I'd spend the summer fishing.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't think it's ever occurred to my father to do something in water other than swim.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You were probably better off... I don't think professional fishing is up your alley...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's probably true...
They see surprise fireworks...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've always liked fireworks...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: They're like stars that we can almost touch.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I've always thought of them as symbols of independence and energy.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That too...
And then one day, in the park, Sara and Nick make daisy chains and look up at the clouds.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: So you really don't know what you want to do with your life?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Does anyone in high school know that?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I do. I'm going to swim.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: But what about afterwards? Or in between? What if you get sick of swimming?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hmmm... That's a little harder. My whole life is swimming.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I told you before, Sara... Swimming is what you do, but it's one part of you.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: With you reminding me all the time, how could I forget?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: If you could do anything, what would you do?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Maybe I'd run for public office...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: And if you don't know what you're doing either, you can be the campaign manager for Senator Sara Kessler.
Nick laughs and leans over to kiss her.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: As long as I'm with you, I know I'll be happy...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Me too...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, I've never been so happy in my life. I think I might be...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Might be what?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Um, never mind. Just kiss me, okay?
They share a long, deep kiss that leaves Sara flushed.
Sara gets home from her date with Nick.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Good evening!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You're always so happy after a run.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, uh, I like running...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know, exercise and endorphins and all that...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Just keep up the good work. You're beginning to give even `me` a run for my money...
nodes.text_bbcode: Just keep up the good work. You're beginning to give even [color=#e23b3b][i]me[/i][/color] a run for my money...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hey, Sara... Can you talk to your sister for me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Why? What happened?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: She was having a hard time focusing today. I tried to give her a pep talk, but that made her cry.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Usually, your mom comforts her, but she's at a PTA meeting tonight, and...  You know I'm not good at this stuff.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah, I'll talk to her.
Sara knocks on Emily's door and enters to find her sister sitting on the bed.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What happened between you and dad?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He was getting in my face about my backstroke because I keep making these small mistakes...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He kept talking about all the hard work you've been doing...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And it just made me feel like the swim schedule he's got me on is impossible.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've had days like that. And believe me... Dad's pep talks aren't as 'peppy' as he'd like to think they are.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You mean the part where he says that your future is hanging above your head?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... Pressure much?
Emily giggles.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've had days where it seems impossible. What we do... It isn't easy.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But how do you do it? You're even getting in an extra hour of running!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't want to tell Emily that having a life outside swimming keeps me sane... But I owe her the truth...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I have a secret for dealing with that. It's...
Sara hesitates.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But what if she spills to Dad?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What is it?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I can't tell her.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I keep motivated by...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: So... What do we do now?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Well... It `is` a parking lot.
Nick slides over, closer to Sara.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: We could always `park`, if you know what I mean...
nodes.text_bbcode: We could always [color=#e23b3b][i]park[/i][/color], if you know what I mean...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee. I think I do.
Nick kisses Sara. In the distance, the sky flashes with lightning. Thunder quickly follows...
Rain patters on the windshield...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I was going to have you drive us home, but I don't think so anymore... Not in this storm.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Awww... Are you sure?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Yeah. I don't think you're quite ready for that yet. The roads get slippery in the rain.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: A few more runs around the lamppost...
The next afternoon, Sara and Nick arrive at the beach...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: How much time have we got left?
Nick checks his phone...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: With driving time... About thirty-four minutes before we have to get back...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's like no time at all! What do we do first?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You want to go for a swim?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Actually... Every time I come to the ocean, my dad's here with a stopwatch, keeping track of my times in the water.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: So... Not that.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But I never get to play around in the sand!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I remember when I was really little, I loved playing in the sand. Making sand castles... Finding seashells... Doing cartwheels with Emily...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That all sounds pretty fun. Uh... This may sound weird, but... What is a cartwheel, exactly?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Are you serious? You don't know what a cartwheel is?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Nope. Is it like a dance move?
Nick shakes his hips a little bit.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Check out my cartwheel. There it goes. Wheeling and dealing.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee. Just. Stop.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That's the jealousy talking.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: A cartwheel is a gymnastics move. I'll show you.
Nick takes out his camera.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Hold on. I want to catch this moment...
Nick finds a spot a few yards off.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: It's been a long time since I've done one of these... Here goes!
Sara breaks into a run, sprinting along the beach, picking up speed!
She throws her hands down, and...
For the rest of their short time together, Sara and Nick cram in as much fun as they can...
They build sand castles...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: We should have a moat!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Typical Kessler. Trying to set up a place where she can swim.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Do I need to mention how you converted the dungeon into a dark room?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: They're practically the same thing!
They collect shells...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Look how pretty this is!
Nick takes a picture. She looks at it.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick! This is just a picture of me! Get one of my shell too!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Okay, okay, fine, Miss Bossy.
And Nick buries Sara's legs in the sand, forcing her to close her eyes as he works on something.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't know if this qualifies as fun...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Just give me a minute... Aaaaaand... Open!
Sara opens her eyes. Nick has constructed a long tail out of sand, extending from Sara's waist.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You make for one heck of a mermaid.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hee...
He takes a picture.
An alarm on his phone goes off.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Time to go...
Nick lifts Sara out of the sand, and the two of them head toward the car...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Sara, I... I want to tell you something.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's about the way I feel about you...
Sara blushes.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: It's just... I've never felt this way about anyone.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I'm... I'm feeling the same way.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: And... Uh... And... Yeah. That's it.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, I'm really glad you said that. It isn't easy telling someone...
Sara sticks the landing!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: `I did it!`
Nick comes running up, embracing her tightly!

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: That looked so cool!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Did you get the photo?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I got a perfect shot with just a little bit of blur so you can really `see` the motion...
nodes.text_bbcode: I got a perfect shot with just a little bit of blur so you can really [color=#e23b3b][i]see[/i][/color] the motion...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Check it out.
Nick shows Sara the photo... Sara's form is perfect... She looks like the spoke in a bicycle wheel.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Beautiful.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You mean me? Or the picture?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Oh, I definitely mean you.
He leans down and kisses her. After a long time, they part...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: As much I'd love doing that forever, I think we should do more here at the beach than just make out and do cartwheels.
Nick shakes his hips again...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: { My cartwheel brings all the girls to the beach! {

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Okay. Yes. I'll do anything if it means you not doing that.
And for the rest of summer, Nick and Sara steal the hour after her practice and spend time together...
They look at shops at the mall...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I've discovered where independent thought and free will go to die.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But at least they die fashionably...
They pick flowers around the lake after her father drives off...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: My parents used to have a lake house, and I'd spend the summer fishing.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't think it's ever occurred to my father to do something in water other than swim.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: You were probably better off... I don't think professional fishing is up your alley...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That's probably true...
They see surprise fireworks...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've always liked fireworks...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: They're like stars that we can almost touch.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I've always thought of them as symbols of independence and energy.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: That too...
And then one day, in the park, Sara and Nick make daisy chains and look up at the clouds.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: So you really don't know what you want to do with your life?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Does anyone in high school know that?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I do. I'm going to swim.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: But what about afterwards? Or in between? What if you get sick of swimming?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hmmm... That's a little harder. My whole life is swimming.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: I told you before, Sara... Swimming is what you do, but it's one part of you.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: With you reminding me all the time, how could I forget?

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: If you could do anything, what would you do?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Maybe I'd run for public office...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: And if you don't know what you're doing either, you can be the campaign manager for Senator Sara Kessler.
Nick laughs and leans over to kiss her.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: As long as I'm with you, I know I'll be happy...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Me too...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Nick, I've never been so happy in my life. I think I might be...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Might be what?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Um, never mind. Just kiss me, okay?
They share a long, deep kiss that leaves Sara flushed.
Sara gets home from her date with Nick.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Good evening!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You're always so happy after a run.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Oh, uh, I like running...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know, exercise and endorphins and all that...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Just keep up the good work. You're beginning to give even `me` a run for my money...
nodes.text_bbcode: Just keep up the good work. You're beginning to give even [color=#e23b3b][i]me[/i][/color] a run for my money...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hey, Sara... Can you talk to your sister for me?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Why? What happened?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: She was having a hard time focusing today. I tried to give her a pep talk, but that made her cry.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Usually, your mom comforts her, but she's at a PTA meeting tonight, and...  You know I'm not good at this stuff.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah, I'll talk to her.
Sara knocks on Emily's door and enters to find her sister sitting on the bed.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: What happened between you and dad?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He was getting in my face about my backstroke because I keep making these small mistakes...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: He kept talking about all the hard work you've been doing...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And it just made me feel like the swim schedule he's got me on is impossible.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've had days like that. And believe me... Dad's pep talks aren't as 'peppy' as he'd like to think they are.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You mean the part where he says that your future is hanging above your head?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Yeah... Pressure much?
Emily giggles.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I've had days where it seems impossible. What we do... It isn't easy.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: But how do you do it? You're even getting in an extra hour of running!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't want to tell Emily that having a life outside swimming keeps me sane... But I owe her the truth...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I have a secret for dealing with that. It's...
Sara hesitates.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: But what if she spills to Dad?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What is it?

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I can't tell her.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I keep motivated by...

args.text: Achieving a grade of A or higher will unlock a special scene.
You have reached the end of `The Storm, Part 1.`
No one knows exactly what happens right before you go...
But some say that you see your life play out like a movie before you...
You were perfect up there...
Well, I couldn't have done it without your help...
Thank you so much for everything you've done...
I've never had anyone believe in me the way you have...
I didn't think I could do this, but with you by my side, I...
Sara feels suddenly warm and bright. Her heartbeat quickens.
For one moment, she looks up at Nick's face and wonders...
Life's little moments pass by...
Magnified by the unknown future that looms ahead...
You said it yourself. My dad doesn't define who I am. Besides, I might have been using him as an excuse.
An excuse for what?
Because I'm scared. Maybe I can be a Princess, or a President, or a friend...
But I don't know anything about being a girlfriend...
It's not like I have the greatest track record either.
But we can figure it out together.
Underneath a flowering tree, Nick draws Sara close. They share a kiss under the stars.
Every important memory flashes before you...
He touches his forehead to hers.
I love the way you laugh... The way your eyes narrow when you're upset...
I love how you make me feel...
I love being around you...
Sara's heart lifts.
I love you, Sara Kessler.
Sara kisses Nick, throwing her entire heart into it.
Until at last...
It all fades away...

nodes.text: The car rounds the lamppost, and Sara brings it back to their original parking spot with ease.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: Great job, Sara. I should have known you'd be a fast learner.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Thanks for taking me out here, Nick.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: I don't have a lot of boyfriends who would trust me enough to coast around a parking lot in their car.

nodes.speaker: Nick
nodes.text: How many boyfriends do you have?!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You know what I mean!
Sara gives Nick a playful punch in the arm. In the distance, dark clouds begin to form in the sky...

nodes.title: The Storm, Part 1
nodes.subtitle: What can you do in an hour?

nodes.text: It's a clear Saturday afternoon, and Sara Kessler is training in the cool waters of the lake.
She takes one stroke after another, slicing cleanly through.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: The shore... I'm almost there...
A few seconds later, she reaches the beach and pulls herself out.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Huff... Huff...
Her younger sister, Emily, splashes onshore a minute later.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Huff... Huff...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sara, you're so fast!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You're amazing!

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Thanks... You're not so bad yourself.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah right! I was leagues behind you! No wonder you broke the national record.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I hope that I can be as fast as you one day.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Hey, you might even be faster.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Not without a `lot` of work.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: Which you're doing. You're a good swimmer.

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: You're good enough now that Dad started letting you train in the lake with me, aren't you?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, I guess...

nodes.speaker: Sara
nodes.text: She looks like she could use some cheering up...
